newsitem.title: INDIA: Foreign fund buying helps Bombay stocks close up.
newsitem.headline: Foreign fund buying helps Bombay stocks close up.

text.p: Shares at Bombay bourses finished higher on Thursday in a session that largely lacked direction, but select buying interest by foreign funds helped blue chips inch ahead near the close, dealers said.
"Fund action was typically in multinational stocks, a lot of fresh positions are slowly being created," said Dilip Joshi, equities dealer at Prime Brokerage, a domestic firm.
The Bombay Stock Exchange's 30-share index ended below the 3,500 mark, adding 7.21 points to a provisional 3,490.69.
"The index movement was not much, but we saw some brisk trading activity," said a dealer at a foreign brokerage.
Marketmen said funds were active buyers in stocks such as Hindustan Petroleum, Bharat Petroleum, Cipla, Oriental Bank, Indian Hotels, Hindalco, Castrol and Siemens.
Prime's Joshi said he was bullish on the market. "People who have a bearish view are only sitting on the fence. Deliveries are getting absorbed at these levels."

"The recent correction in the Indian stock market provides foreign investors the opportunity to accumulate holdings in what has, so far, been a domestically driven rally," Christopher Wood, Peregrine's emerging markets strategist in Hong Kong, said in the company's latest India market strategy report.
Peregrine Securities advised foreign investors to consolidate holdings in Indian stocks on the back of improved liquidity, broader market participation and cheap valuations.
"Favoured sectors include banks, capital goods, consumer non-durables, computer software and oil refining," Wood said.
Indian shares were likely to show a rise despite being the best performing market among Asian markets so far this year, he added. "Valuations remain comparatively attractive."
At the BSE, Reliance added 0.50 rupees to 271.75,SBI 0.25 to 277.50, ITC 2.25 to 419.0 and Bharat Petroleum 12.0 to 382.0.
